newsitem.title: USA: Lincoln Q2 oper profit up before charge.
newsitem.headline: Lincoln Q2 oper profit up before charge.

text.p: Life insurer Lincoln National Corp on Wednesday reported a second quarter operating profit, excluding a large charge the company took to strengthen its disability income reserves.
However, Lincoln National reported a second quarter net loss when including the special charge.
Lincoln National said it took a $130 million, or $1.24 a share, after-tax charge to strengthen reserves for individual disability income insurance.
The Fort Wayne, Indiana-based insurer said it believes further charges for this block of disability income business are unlikely.
Before this charge, the company had already strengthened disability income reserves twice in the last four years by a total of $121.6 million after tax.

"After the strengthening, we believe that the assumptions underlying our reserves are such that further charges are unlikely in the foreseeable future for this block of disability income business," Lincoln National chief executive Ian Rolland said.

Lincoln National said it launched an in-depth review of all disability income reserves after second quarter information revealed its experience had deteriorated from assumptions underlying the company's reserves.

Income from operations, which excludes the special charge but includes income from discontinued operations, was $114.5 million in the second quarter, or $1.10 per share, compared with $94.6 million, or $0.90 per share, in the year ago quarter.
That compares with the First Call consensus estimate of $1.03 a share.
Lincoln National shares rose 2-12/16, or more than four percent, to 68-5/8 in late afternoon trading.

Excluding the special charge and the income from discontinued operations, second quarter operating income from continuing operations was $81.9 million, or $0.78 a share, compared with $71.4 million or $0.68 a share a year ago.

Lincoln National said its American States Financial Corp property-casualty and life insurance businesses were reported as discontinued operations in the second quarter even though the sale of the business is not expected to be completed until the third quarter.
Lincoln National in June agreed to sell its 83 percent stake in American States to SAFECO Corp, which will result in proceeds of $2.15 billion after tax.
Alex. Brown analyst John Hall said he did not view the special charge as a negative factor.
"What the charge does, it kind of sets the table for 1998," Hall said, eliminating the drag on future earnings.
